Leakage-Aware Deep Learning for Leukemia Image Classification¶

Complete Experimental Pipeline, Integrity Audit, Cross-Validation Results, and Explainability Analysis¶

Date: 13 September 2026
Models: ConvNeXtV2-Tiny; EfficientNet-B1
Datasets: C-NMC 2019; ALL-IDB1; ALL-IDB2
Locked seed: 42
Outer folds: 5
Total completed fits: 30 / 30
Primary comparison criterion: pooled out-of-fold (OOF) balanced accuracy + MCC, interpreted with fold variability, probabilistic metrics, data-integrity constraints, and dataset-specific limitations.

Scope. This notebook is the master scientific record of the completed experiment. It is a synthesis of the repository's frozen integrity manifests, split files, source code, training histories, completion metadata, OOF predictions, post-training reports, and Grad-CAM outputs. It does not retrain a model or recompute scientific inference.

0. Executive overview¶

Research objective¶

The project asks whether two ImageNet-pretrained convolutional architectures—ConvNeXtV2-Tiny and EfficientNet-B1—can distinguish leukemia-associated from non-leukemia-associated microscopy images under a deliberately leakage-aware cross-validation design. The three datasets represent different image units and therefore require different grouping and interpretation rules: C-NMC is a cell-image dataset with subject identifiers, ALL-IDB1 contains full blood-smear fields, and ALL-IDB2 contains crops reconstructed back to ALL-IDB1 source fields.

Design in one paragraph¶

Three datasets × two models × five outer folds × one seed gives 30 completed fits. The outer fold is reserved for OOF evaluation. Checkpoint selection occurs on an inner validation partition constructed only from the outer-training portion. Duplicates and related observations are controlled at the strongest identifier available: C-NMC uses subject plus decoded-pixel duplicate connectivity; ALL-IDB1 keeps canonical full fields disjoint; ALL-IDB2 keeps all crops from a reconstructed source parent field together. Class weights are derived only from inner-training labels, augmentation is training-only, and the outer-held-out fold is not used to choose a checkpoint. Training accuracy was recorded at every epoch for all 30 fits; however, final performance claims are based on held-out pooled OOF evaluation rather than training-set accuracy.

Main result¶

ConvNeXtV2-Tiny is the preferred architecture within this locked experiment because it has the higher pooled OOF balanced accuracy and MCC at every reported evaluation unit. This is metric-specific, not blanket dominance: for example, C-NMC cell-level NLL is slightly lower for EfficientNet (0.7508) than ConvNeXt (0.7595), and EfficientNet has C-NMC subject sensitivity 1.0000 versus ConvNeXt 0.9787.

Main limitations¶

The study uses a single seed; fold SD is descriptive fold-to-fold variability, not a confidence interval or multi-seed uncertainty. There is no independent external cohort. ALL-IDB1 has severe acquisition/resolution confounding. ALL-IDB1 and ALL-IDB2 share source material, so ALL-IDB2 is not independent external validation of ALL-IDB1. Patient/specimen identities are unavailable for both ALL-IDB datasets. Both C-NMC training series show HIGH overfitting tendency despite best-checkpoint selection.

Explainability conclusion¶

Grad-CAM was generated only for locked OOF samples with the matching outer-fold best checkpoint. It provides a descriptive spatial diagnostic, not a causal explanation. Selected C-NMC ConvNeXt false negatives were frequently peripheral/background-heavy; ALL-IDB1 showed recurrent edge/padding-adjacent or field-wide activation; ALL-IDB2 showed mixed cell-overlap and surrounding-field activation. These patterns do not prove morphology learning, biological causality, or causal feature use.

0.1 Detailed end-to-end pipeline schematic¶

The figure below summarizes the complete leakage-aware workflow for all three datasets and both deep-learning architectures, from dataset integrity controls through preprocessing, training-only augmentation, grouped five-fold cross-validation, checkpoint selection, pooled OOF evaluation, and Grad-CAM-based comparison.

Figure 0.2 — Overall leukemia classification pipeline for three datasets and two deep-learning models. Dataset-specific grouping prevents known leakage routes; deterministic D4 augmentation is restricted to inner-training samples; checkpoints are selected without using the outer-held-out fold; and final comparisons use pooled OOF predictions at each dataset's scientifically appropriate evaluation unit.

1. Research question and evaluation units¶

1.1 What “leukemia image classification” means here¶

The binary target is dataset-specific but consistently encoded with the non-ALL/healthy class as 0 and the ALL-associated class as 1. For C-NMC, HEM = 0, ALL = 1, and the reported positive-class probability is P(ALL) = softmax[:, 1]. ALL-IDB1 uses healthy_field = 0, all_field = 1; ALL-IDB2 uses the analogous negative/positive crop label.

1.2 Why the evaluation unit matters¶

Dataset Native image unit Scientifically meaningful grouping Reported evaluation unit(s)
C-NMC Cropped cell image Subject plus exact decoded-pixel duplicate connectivity Cell; subject
ALL-IDB1 Full microscopy field Canonical full field / duplicate component Field
ALL-IDB2 Cell/region crop Reconstructed canonical ALL-IDB1 source parent field Crop; parent-field

An image-level random split would be unsafe whenever multiple images are biologically or visually related. Duplicate images can appear in different supplied folders; many C-NMC cells come from the same subject; and multiple ALL-IDB2 crops originate from one parent field. A model evaluated on a related image from a training group could appear to generalize while exploiting shared acquisition, background, subject, or source-field information. The cross-validation unit therefore follows the strongest known relationship, not simply the file row.

6.2 Exact-byte and decoded-pixel duplicate audit¶

The audit deliberately distinguishes file identity from decoded image identity:

  • Exact file hash: SHA-256 over exact file bytes.
  • Decoded-pixel hash: hash of decoded pixel content, able to reveal image equality even if file containers/metadata differ.

The exact-byte audit found 106 duplicate groups / 212 files, all size two. There were 0 exact-file duplicate groups crossing top-level challenge phases, but 94 exact-file duplicate pairs crossed the supplied training-fold boundaries. Additional within-fold exact duplicates were present (5 in supplied training fold 1, 5 in supplied training fold 2, 2 in final test), with 0 labeled duplicate label mismatches.

The decoded-pixel audit exposed six additional train↔preliminary relationships that were not byte-identical. Those six cross-phase paired relationships imply 12 endpoints, so six training images and their six preliminary counterparts were quarantined with reason:

exact_decoded_pixel_duplicate_crosses_challenge_phase

Final phase-specific eligibility is therefore:

Phase Raw Eligible Excluded/quarantined
Training/development 10,661 10,655 6
Preliminary 1,867 1,861 6
Final unlabeled test 2,586 2,586 0 in its own phase context

The inventory/audit records 112 decoded-pixel duplicate relationships/groups in total; pair-level inspection separates 106 byte-identical relationships from the six pixel-identical cross-phase relationships. The scientific unit is important: six relationships, twelve quarantined endpoints.

6.4 C-NMC limitations of the integrity audit¶

The integrity checks establish file-byte and decoded-pixel equality plus subject/group isolation. They do not prove absence of perceptually near-identical images because no exhaustive perceptual-hash/SSIM near-duplicate scan is part of the frozen C-NMC protocol. Duplicate images retained within development are grouped rather than necessarily deduplicated, so image-level metrics can still give more weight to repeated content within a group. The preliminary split is locked, and the final test split is unlabeled; neither contributes to the reported supervised OOF metrics.

8.3 Interpretation boundary¶

ConvNeXt's perfect field-level OOF result is dataset-level performance under strong acquisition confounding. It cannot be interpreted as proof that the model learned leukemia morphology, nor as evidence of biological causality. Stable performance across field-disjoint folds does not eliminate a confound that is distributed across the entire dataset.

The repository does not contain a finalized scientific artifact for the approximate “metadata-only nuisance baseline” figures mentioned during development (~85.05% accuracy / ~83.67% balanced accuracy). Because those values cannot be traced to a frozen report or result file, they are not promoted to an authoritative result in this master notebook. The verified class-by-resolution structure and the nuisance-stratified OOF table above are the reproducible confounding evidence.

9. ALL-IDB2 integrity, parent reconstruction, and adjudication¶

9.1 Raw and eligible crops¶

The raw inventory contains 260 RGB TIFF crops, exactly balanced at 130 positive and 130 negative. Of these, 250 are standard 257×257 crops and 10 have irregular dimensions. Frozen eligibility retains 258 crops: 130 positive + 128 negative; 248 retained crops are standard 257×257 and 10 are irregular.

The exact duplicate Im223_0 == Im257_0 is resolved by retaining 223 and excluding 257. Near-duplicate/source-content review additionally resolves the following candidate pairs:

Pair Decision
028 / 031 Distinct; mapped to different parents; retain both
138 / 146 Distinct; mapped to different parents; retain both
222 / 256 Same source content / overlapping pixel-identical crop; retain 222, exclude 256
223 / 257 Exact duplicate; retain 223, exclude 257

Eligibility therefore contains 253 ordinary ELIGIBLE, five RESTORED_ELIGIBLE, and two EXCLUDED decisions.

9.2 Parent-field reconstruction¶

All 260/260 raw crops were reconstructed to 102 canonical ALL-IDB1 parent fields using allidb_full_resolution_template_ncc_v1. The parent-map file uses column allidb1_parent_sample_id (not source_parent_id). Its SHA-256 recorded in the eligibility decision is:

F04D6DE9F6B8C6C3542CC8A77B0D77411E5901B2CC4FE47CE50ADFB6BD73841B

All 260 mappings are REPRODUCED_HIGH_CONFIDENCE; all have manual_review_status = NOT_REVIEWED. Full-resolution NCC is extremely high:

  • minimum = 0.999991893768
  • median = 1.0
  • maximum = 1.0

Runner-up gap:

  • minimum = 0.005358457565
  • median = 0.1777936518195
  • maximum = 0.572860211134

The implementation acceptance thresholds are NCC ≥ 0.999 and runner-up gap ≥ 0.003. A direct inventory/parent-map join found 0 mapped-label disagreements across the raw 260 mappings.

Among the final 258 eligible crops, the 102 source parents comprise 58 negative parents and 44 positive parents.

Caution: reconstruction is algorithmically very high-confidence but was not manually adjudicated crop-by-crop. The mapping evidence is therefore strong computational provenance, not a claim of independent human verification.

10. ALL-IDB2 leakage prevention and relationship to ALL-IDB1¶

A naïve crop-level random split would be scientifically invalid because multiple crops from a single microscopy field share source pixels, acquisition conditions, staining context, and local background. All crops from one reconstructed source field therefore remain together in the same outer fold.

Required scientific wording: parent-field-disjoint cross-validation over ALL-IDB2 crops mapped to canonical ALL-IDB1 source fields; patient and specimen identities are unavailable.

Two interpretation boundaries follow immediately:

  1. Parent-field metrics are not patient-level metrics. The parent identifier represents a source field, not a verified patient/specimen.
  2. ALL-IDB1 and ALL-IDB2 share source material. ALL-IDB2 is therefore not independent external validation of ALL-IDB1. They are complementary analyses of related material.

12. Cross-validation and inner model-selection design¶

12.1 Outer versus inner roles¶

The design is “nested-style” model selection rather than an outer fold reused for tuning:

  • Outer fold: held out for final OOF evaluation for that fit.
  • Outer-training partition: the only pool from which inner training and inner validation are constructed.
  • Inner validation: monitors model selection, early stopping, and checkpoint ranking.
  • Best checkpoint: reloaded and evaluated once on that fold's outer-held-out rows to generate the OOF CSV.

12.2 Split algorithms¶

C-NMC. The outer split is a frozen 5-fold manifest over leakage-aware final_group_id groups. The inner split is not SGKF: it is a deterministic group-preserving hashed allocation of outer-training groups, using approximately 20% for validation while keeping final groups intact. The inner seed follows seed*1000 + outer_fold*10 + 7, giving 42007, 42017, 42027, 42037, 42047.

ALL-IDB1. Outer: StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42), group = canonical field/duplicate component, stratum = label | resolution_family. Inner: 2-fold SGKF using the same field grouping, deterministic split 0, with seed 42007 + 10 × outer_fold.

ALL-IDB2. Outer: 5-fold shuffled SGKF, group = source parent field, stratum = label | standard_crop. Inner: 2-fold SGKF with the same parent grouping, deterministic split 0, seed 42007 + 10 × outer_fold.

13. Why the design avoids the known leakage modes¶

Leakage / bias route Control in the final protocol Residual limitation
1. Exact file duplicates SHA-256 inventory and canonicalization/grouping Equality audit is not a perceptual-near-duplicate guarantee
2. Pixel-identical duplicates Decoded-pixel hash; cross-phase C-NMC pairs quarantined; related dev samples grouped Related but non-identical images may remain
3. Near duplicates ALL-IDB2 near-duplicate candidates explicitly adjudicated C-NMC has no exhaustive perceptual near-duplicate scan
4. C-NMC subject leakage Subject IDs kept outer-fold disjoint; duplicate-connected subjects merged via final_group_id Subject-level fold counts are small
5. ALL-IDB2 parent-field leakage All crops from one reconstructed parent remain together Parent is not a patient identifier
6. ALL-IDB1 field leakage Canonical full fields are outer-fold disjoint Patient/specimen identity unavailable
7. Challenge phase leakage Cross-phase pixel-identical C-NMC endpoints quarantined; preliminary/final not used for supervised OOF C-NMC final labels unavailable
8. Augmentation leakage D4 augmentation applied only to inner training Augmentation does not fix confounding
9. Class-weight leakage Weights computed only from inner-training labels Single weighting formula tested
10. Checkpoint-selection leakage Selection uses only inner validation Inner split is one deterministic selection per outer fold
11. Outer-fold tuning Outer fold untouched during checkpoint selection No independent external cohort after CV
12. OOF integrity Each OOF row produced only when its sample is outer-held-out Single seed only
13. Explainability leakage Grad-CAM sample uses its own outer-fold best_checkpoint.pt Runtime single-sample probabilities can differ slightly from batched OOF probabilities; locked class is authoritative
14. Fitted preprocessing statistics No dataset normalization/statistic is fitted from held-out data; fixed ImageNet mean/std used Source acquisition differences persist
15. ALL-IDB independence Explicitly no independence claim between ALL-IDB1 and ALL-IDB2 Shared provenance remains a generalization limitation

14. Preprocessing¶

The final behavior is taken directly from src/data/preprocessing.py.

14.1 C-NMC¶

RGB → direct bicubic resize to model input size → tensor → ImageNet normalization

  • ConvNeXt: 224×224.
  • EfficientNet: 240×240.
  • No aspect-ratio preservation in the primary C-NMC path.

14.2 ALL-IDB1 / ALL-IDB2¶

RGB → aspect-preserving bicubic fit → ImageNet-mean padding → tensor → ImageNet normalization

The original aspect ratio is preserved by resizing the field/crop to fit inside the square target. The remaining canvas is padded with an RGB value derived from the ImageNet mean. This avoids geometric stretching but introduces explicit padded regions. Those regions are scientifically relevant to the interpretability analysis because edge/padding sensitivity could become an acquisition-correlated cue, especially in ALL-IDB1.

14.3 Fixed normalization¶

ImageNet normalization uses mean (0.485, 0.456, 0.406) and standard deviation (0.229, 0.224, 0.225). These are fixed constants, not statistics estimated from the study datasets.

14.4 Stain/contrast methods not used in the primary experiment¶

The codebase contains optional CLAHE support, but the locked primary configs disable it. No CLAHE and no Macenko stain normalization are part of the primary analyses summarized here.

15. Training-only augmentation¶

The augmentation module implements the eight-element dihedral group D4:

identity, rot90, rot180, rot270, hflip, vflip, transpose, transverse

Transform selection is deterministic and label-independent. A SHA-256-based selection key includes dataset, seed, outer fold, epoch, and an opaque sample key; the label is deliberately excluded. Augmentation is applied only to inner-training samples. Inner validation and outer-held-out OOF evaluation use deterministic preprocessing without D4 augmentation.

This choice increases orientation diversity without introducing stochastic validation transforms or label-conditioned transform selection.

16. Model architectures and pretrained initialization¶

16.1 ConvNeXtV2-Tiny¶

  • Timm identifier: convnextv2_tiny.fcmae_ft_in1k
  • Pretrained initialization: enabled.
  • Model construction: timm feature extractor (num_classes=0) followed by a project Linear(768, 2) classifier.
  • Input: 224×224.
  • Enforced trainable parameter count: 27,868,034.
  • Grad-CAM target: backbone.stages[-1].blocks[-1]; verified activation shape 1×768×7×7.

16.2 EfficientNet-B1¶

  • Timm identifier: tf_efficientnet_b1.aa_in1k
  • Pretrained initialization: enabled.
  • Model construction: timm classifier with two outputs and dropout 0.2.
  • Input: 240×240.
  • Enforced trainable parameter count: 6,515,746.
  • Grad-CAM target: model.conv_head; verified activation shape 1×1280×8×8.

The experiment compares complete training pipelines under fixed dataset-specific preprocessing rather than performing an architecture-mechanism ablation. Therefore a performance difference cannot be causally attributed to a specific block, normalization scheme, parameter count, or feature hierarchy.

17. Loss, class weighting, optimization, scheduling, AMP, and early stopping¶

17.1 Weighted cross-entropy¶

For inner-training class counts (n_c) and total (N), the class-balanced weight is

[ w_c = \frac{N}{2n_c}. ]

The weights are computed strictly from inner-training labels for each outer-fold fit. Weighted cross-entropy is evaluated in float32 with autocast disabled around the loss calculation for numerical stability. A representative certified ALL-IDB1 ConvNeXt fold-0 manifest records inner-train counts [24, 19] and weights [0.8958333, 1.1315789], which matches the formula.

17.2 Two-phase fine-tuning¶

Training proceeds in two phases:

  1. Warm-up / classifier phase: backbone frozen; classifier/head optimized with AdamW at learning rate 3e-4.
  2. Fine-tuning phase: backbone unfrozen; separate AdamW parameter groups use backbone LR 1e-5 and head LR 1e-4.

Common optimizer settings: AdamW betas (0.9, 0.999), weight decay 1e-4, gradient clipping at norm 1.0.

After warm-up, CosineAnnealingLR runs over the remaining configured epochs with minimum backbone learning rate equal to 10% of the backbone LR. ConvNeXt uses 3 warm-up epochs and a 30-epoch cap; EfficientNet uses 5 warm-up epochs and a 50-epoch cap.

17.3 Batch and accumulation¶

  • ConvNeXt: physical batch size 8, gradient accumulation 2.
  • EfficientNet: physical batch size 8, gradient accumulation 1.
  • DataLoader workers: 0 in the locked training path.
  • DataLoader generator seed follows the deterministic seed/fold construction in the trainer.

17.4 Mixed precision¶

CUDA AMP is enabled in the locked configs. torch.amp autocast and a CUDA GradScaler are used; the configured initial scale is 32768. Checkpoint state includes the scaler state so resume does not silently restart AMP dynamics.

17.5 Early stopping and checkpoint ranking¶

ConvNeXt patience = 8; EfficientNet patience = 10. Early stopping is permitted only after the configured minimum executed epoch count (11 for ConvNeXt, 15 for EfficientNet).

Candidate checkpoints are ranked lexicographically by:

  1. higher MCC
  2. higher balanced accuracy
  3. lower NLL
  4. earlier epoch

The final OOF prediction is generated from best_checkpoint.pt, not automatically from the terminal epoch.

18. Checkpoint payload, fail-closed resume safety, and protocol locking¶

18.1 Checkpoint contents¶

last_checkpoint.pt is a resumable training state containing the current model state, optimizer state, scheduler state, scaler state, completed/next epoch, best epoch and metrics, best model state, early-stop counter, training-finished flag, history, metadata/current phase, Python/NumPy/CPU/CUDA RNG states, DataLoader generator state, and optional resume provenance.

best_checkpoint.pt is the scientific model-selection artifact: best model state plus fit metadata, best epoch, and best validation metrics.

18.2 Resume behavior¶

Resume restores optimizer/scheduler/scaler/RNG/DataLoader state rather than merely loading model weights. The trainer validates contiguous history and device/RNG assumptions. A changed code/config context is not silently accepted: compatibility is governed by a reviewed resume_compatibility_v1.json mechanism that checks fit identity, old/new code/config fingerprints, documented semantic equivalence, and reviewed differences.

18.3 Protocol fingerprints¶

src/training/protocol.py fingerprints the scientific configuration, split schema/inventory, outer held-out IDs, inner-split policy, and essential code files. Fit metadata stores:

  • configuration fingerprint
  • scientific/protocol fingerprint
  • code fingerprint
  • outer-held-out sample-ID hash
  • inner-training class counts and class weights

A representative ALL-IDB1 ConvNeXt fold-0 fit_complete.json also records SHA-256 hashes for the best checkpoint, training histories, fit metadata, and OOF CSV. The completion marker is written only after those required artifacts exist.

18.4 Why this matters¶

The protocol is intentionally fail-closed: accidental resume under a scientifically changed split/config/code state is treated as incompatible unless explicitly reviewed. This protects the audit trail from a common failure mode in long-running cross-validation experiments—continuing a partially completed fit under subtly changed assumptions.

19. OOF methodology and metric definitions¶

Exactly 30 OOF CSVs exist: six dataset/model combinations × five folds. Per architecture, pooled OOF row counts are exactly 10,655 C-NMC cells, 107 ALL-IDB1 fields, and 258 ALL-IDB2 crops. The cross-model sets of (sample_id, outer_fold, true_label) match exactly. No leakage-control group spans outer folds.

For a binary label (y\in{0,1}) and positive-class probability (p), the project reports thresholded and probabilistic/discrimination measures:

  • Accuracy.
  • Sensitivity / recall / TPR.
  • Specificity / TNR.
  • Precision and F1.
  • Balanced accuracy: (\frac{TPR+TNR}{2}).
  • Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC).
  • ROC-AUC and PR-AUC.
  • Negative log-likelihood (NLL).
  • Brier score.
  • ECE-10 (10-bin expected calibration error).

Thresholded predictions use 0.5. ROC-AUC/PR-AUC assess ranking across thresholds; NLL/Brier/ECE assess probabilistic behavior. These calibration-related metrics are informative diagnostics, but this experiment is not a separate prospective calibration study and does not choose a clinical operating threshold.

Pooled OOF versus fold summaries¶

The final pooled OOF metric is calculated after concatenating all held-out rows. Separately, the five outer-fold metrics are summarized as arithmetic mean ± sample SD. Because fold sizes and class composition vary, pooled and mean-of-fold values need not be identical.

The fold SD is descriptive heterogeneity across the five folds. It is not a confidence interval, not repeated-CV uncertainty, and not seed-to-seed uncertainty.

20. Dataset-specific probability aggregation¶

20.1 C-NMC subject aggregation¶

Cell probabilities are averaged within subject_id:

[ \bar p_s = \frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i\in s} p_i, \qquad \hat y_s=\mathbf{1}[\bar p_s\ge 0.5]. ]

The pooled subject evaluation contains 73 subjects. This is a genuine subject-level aggregation because subject IDs exist and are outer-fold disjoint.

20.2 ALL-IDB1¶

The native row already represents the full field, so the field itself is the evaluation unit. No subject aggregation is scientifically available.

20.3 ALL-IDB2 parent-field aggregation¶

Crop probabilities are averaged within the canonical source parent field (source_parent_id in OOF artifacts, corresponding to allidb1_parent_sample_id in the parent-map file):

[ \bar p_f = \frac{1}{n_f}\sum_{i\in f} p_i, \qquad \hat y_f=\mathbf{1}[\bar p_f\ge 0.5]. ]

The 258 eligible crops aggregate to 102 parent fields; parent labels were internally consistent. This is parent-field evaluation, not patient-level evaluation.

Training vs Inner-Validation vs Held-Out OOF Performance¶

The evaluation hierarchy is:

TRAINING → INNER VALIDATION → BEST CHECKPOINT → OUTER HELD-OUT FOLD → POOLED OOF GENERALIZATION

Training metrics¶

Training metrics are calculated on the samples used for gradient updates in the current inner-training partition. They monitor optimization, convergence, and training-versus-validation gaps. Training accuracy is not a generalization estimate. The repository audit verified train_accuracy in 30/30 training_history.csv files, covering 1,036 epoch rows with no missing, null, NaN, or infinite values. The histories also record train_balanced_accuracy and train_mcc.

Inner-validation metrics¶

Inner-validation metrics are calculated on a validation subset carved only from the outer-training partition. They are used for checkpoint and best-epoch selection. They are therefore model-selection metrics, not the final held-out result. In the table below, “Best Inner-Validation Accuracy” means the validation accuracy at the repository-recorded selected best checkpoint in each fold, followed by mean ± sample SD across the five folds; it is not the independent maximum of val_accuracy over all epochs.

Outer-held-out / OOF metrics¶

For each outer fold, the evaluation samples were excluded from both gradient updates and checkpoint selection. Each eligible sample therefore receives one out-of-fold prediction from a model that did not train on that sample and did not use it for checkpoint selection. Concatenating the five outer-fold predictions produces the pooled OOF metrics used as the study's primary cross-validated generalization estimates.

Core accuracy comparison¶

Training and inner-validation entries are mean ± sample SD across 5 folds. Pooled OOF entries are single pooled values and therefore are not shown with ± values.

Dataset Model Best-Epoch Training Accuracy Best Inner-Validation Accuracy Final-Epoch Training Accuracy Pooled Held-Out OOF Accuracy Higher-Level Aggregated OOF Accuracy Interpretation

C-NMC 2019 EfficientNet-B1 0.9074 ± 0.0940 0.8524 ± 0.0700 0.9551 ± 0.0220 0.8617 (cell) 0.8767 subject-level OOF HIGH overfitting classification; terminal training accuracy is substantially above held-out cell OOF accuracy.
ALL-IDB1 ConvNeXtV2-Tiny 1.0000 ± 0.0000 1.0000 ± 0.0000 1.0000 ± 0.0000 1.0000 (field) N/A — native field is already the evaluation unit Perfect internal field-level classification occurs in a strongly acquisition/resolution-confounded dataset.
ALL-IDB1 EfficientNet-B1 0.9341 ± 0.0451 0.9908 ± 0.0126 0.9478 ± 0.0518 0.9720 (field) N/A — native field is already the evaluation unit Strong internal field-level OOF performance; interpretation remains limited by acquisition/resolution confounding.
ALL-IDB2 ConvNeXtV2-Tiny 1.0000 ± 0.0000 0.9870 ± 0.0094 1.0000 ± 0.0000 0.9845 (crop) 1.0000 parent-field OOF Strong crop-level OOF performance and perfect parent-field aggregation; overfitting classification remains MODERATE.
ALL-IDB2 EfficientNet-B1 0.9431 ± 0.0204 0.8936 ± 0.0168 0.9572 ± 0.0312 0.8992 (crop) 0.9510 parent-field OOF Training accuracy exceeds crop-level OOF accuracy; parent-field aggregation improves the held-out estimate.

Very high training accuracy is common in high-capacity fine-tuned CNNs and demonstrates that the optimizer can fit the inner-training data. It does not establish generalization. Large training-versus-inner-validation or training-versus-OOF gaps are evidence of overfitting tendency. C-NMC is the clearest example: ConvNeXt reaches approximately 0.993 best-checkpoint training accuracy and 0.998 final-epoch training accuracy, while pooled held-out cell OOF accuracy is 0.9094. That separation is consistent with the previously reported HIGH overfitting classification. The scientifically relevant final performance claim is the outer-held-out pooled OOF result, not final-epoch training accuracy.

Is this test accuracy?¶

The project does not contain a separate fixed labeled external test cohort. Instead, each sample used for the reported evaluation is assessed exactly once in an outer fold by a model that did not train on that sample and did not use that sample for checkpoint selection. The pooled outer-fold predictions therefore provide the study's cross-validated held-out generalization estimate. In this notebook these values are referred to as Held-Out OOF Accuracy, not external test accuracy.

  • C-NMC Final is unlabeled; accuracy cannot be computed for it.
  • C-NMC Preliminary was not used as a fresh final test set.
  • C-NMC development evaluation is subject/group-disjoint cross-validation.
  • ALL-IDB1 is field-disjoint cross-validation over canonical full fields; patient/specimen identifiers are unavailable.
  • ALL-IDB2 is parent-field-disjoint cross-validation; patient/specimen identifiers are unavailable, and parent-field metrics are not subject-level metrics.
  • ALL-IDB1 and ALL-IDB2 share source provenance and must not be described as independent external validation cohorts.

    ("cnmc", "convnextv2_tiny", "C-NMC — ConvNeXtV2-Tiny"),

    ("allidb1", "efficientnet_b1", "ALL-IDB1 — EfficientNet-B1"),

        local_handles.append(Line2D([0], [0], color=train_line.get_color(), lw=1.8, label=f"Fold {int(fold)}"))
    if not fold_handles:

plt.show()

23. Best epochs, training behavior, and overfitting¶

Dataset Model Mean best epoch Range Epoch cap Overfitting assessment
C-NMC ConvNeXt 20.0 13–28 30 HIGH
C-NMC EfficientNet 22.8 6–41 50 HIGH
ALL-IDB1 ConvNeXt 30.0 30–30 30 LOW
ALL-IDB1 EfficientNet 37.6 31–48 50 MODERATE
ALL-IDB2 ConvNeXt 17.4 12–24 30 MODERATE
ALL-IDB2 EfficientNet 40.2 28–49 50 MODERATE

The configured “max epochs” is an upper bound; histories may stop early. The overfitting classification used training-history diagnostics: HIGH when end-versus-best NLL regret exceeded 0.15 together with substantial MCC regret or train–validation MCC gap; MODERATE at lower deterioration thresholds; otherwise LOW.

For C-NMC ConvNeXt, all five folds were classified HIGH; the overfitting audit found substantial terminal deterioration relative to each fold's best validation-NLL point together with train–validation metric gaps. EfficientNet was HIGH overall (three HIGH, two MODERATE folds). This overfitting diagnostic is distinct from the repository's lexicographically selected checkpoint epoch. Best-checkpoint selection therefore matters: the OOF metrics are not terminal-epoch metrics. However, checkpoint selection does not erase the observed overfitting tendency or substitute for external validation.

ALL-IDB1 ConvNeXt is different: classification MCC/BA first reached 1.0 at epochs 11, 8, 18, 10, and 9, while validation NLL continued improving through epoch 30. Its epoch-30 selections reflect probability-loss improvement after classification saturation, not 30 epochs of continuing class-separation gains.

24. Grad-CAM methodology and OOF safety¶

24.1 Primary analysis¶

The six primary trees were generated by scripts/run_gradcam_analysis.py, not by the legacy scripts/run_gradcam.py. Each dataset/model pair contains 25 deterministic OOF cases (150 primary CAMs total), selected from the locked pooled OOF table without image inspection. Selection balances TP/TN/FP/FN; if total errors are ≤6, all errors are included and remaining slots are balanced across correct cases. ALL-IDB1 additionally balances by resolution_family.

Each selected sample is checked against its recorded outer fold and explained using that fold's canonical best_checkpoint.pt. The CAM target is the locked OOF predicted class.

For FP/FN cases the Grad-CAM therefore explains activation associated with the incorrect predicted class, not the ground-truth class.

24.2 Primary selection counts¶

Dataset Model N TP TN FP FN
C-NMC ConvNeXt 25 7 6 6 6
C-NMC EfficientNet 25 7 6 6 6
ALL-IDB1 ConvNeXt 25 13 12 0 0
ALL-IDB1 EfficientNet 25 11 11 2 1
ALL-IDB2 ConvNeXt 25 11 10 1 3
ALL-IDB2 EfficientNet 25 7 6 6 6

All five source folds are represented in every primary pair directory.

24.3 Border-attention metric¶

The raw CAM is converted to a finite, nonnegative normalized heatmap in exact model-input geometry. The outer 10% of input width and height on all four sides defines the border. border_energy_fraction is the fraction of total normalized CAM energy within that border; the complement is center energy. Metrics are computed from the raw heatmap—not the colored overlay.

Because input sizes differ, the discrete border mask occupies slightly different image fractions (approximately 36.85% at 224 and 36.0% at 240). Absolute cross-architecture CAM metrics are therefore diagnostic, not a paired inferential comparison.

27. Explainability limitations and generation-provenance caveat¶

The primary Grad-CAM summaries are outcome-stratified representative samples, not prevalence-weighted estimates over every OOF row. Cross-model selected-ID overlap is only 1/25 for C-NMC, 6/25 for ALL-IDB1, and 3/25 for ALL-IDB2, so architecture comparisons are largely unpaired. Native CAM resolution is coarse (7×7 ConvNeXt; 8×8 EfficientNet) before interpolation. No stain segmentation, cell segmentation, or padding segmentation was used.

The generated outputs contain one reproducibility discrepancy that must be preserved in the audit trail:

  • Current scripts/run_gradcam_analysis.py hard-codes runtime probability tolerance 0.05.
  • Generated ConvNeXt primary summaries record tolerance 0.001.
  • Generated EfficientNet summaries record tolerance 0.05.

Therefore the current source file is not an exact generation snapshot for the ConvNeXt primary Grad-CAM outputs. The generated summaries/manifests remain the source of truth for those completed outputs. This discrepancy affects reproducibility provenance, not the locked OOF predictions themselves.

The older scripts/run_gradcam.py has different semantics (first-N outer-development samples, fixed target class 1, original-image metric space). It must not be used to describe the six primary Grad-CAM trees; only run_gradcam_analysis.py defines the primary analysis semantics.

28. Study limitations¶

  1. Single random seed (42). No seed-to-seed uncertainty is estimated.
  2. No independent external test cohort. Reported numbers are cross-validated OOF estimates inside the available development data.
  3. C-NMC final test remains unlabeled and untouched. C-NMC results are internal development estimates, not challenge-test estimates.
  4. C-NMC overfitting tendency is HIGH for both architectures. Best-checkpoint selection limits terminal deterioration but does not remove the concern.
  5. C-NMC fold heterogeneity is substantial, especially subject specificity; subject folds contain only 13–17 subjects.
  6. C-NMC integrity does not include an exhaustive perceptual near-duplicate scan. Exact byte/pixel equality is controlled; more subtle visual relatedness can remain.
  7. ALL-IDB1 has strong acquisition/resolution confounding. All 33 eligible 1712×1368 fields are positive.
  8. ALL-IDB1 and ALL-IDB2 share source provenance. They are not independent external validation datasets.
  9. ALL-IDB1/2 lack patient and specimen identifiers. Subject-disjoint claims are unsupported.
  10. ALL-IDB2 parent-field aggregation is not patient-level evaluation. It aggregates source fields only.
  11. ALL-IDB2 parent reconstruction is algorithmic. All 260 mappings are high-confidence but NOT_REVIEWED manually.
  12. Fold SD is not a confidence interval and not repeated-seed/repeated-CV uncertainty.
  13. Grad-CAM is post-hoc and non-causal. It does not prove causal feature use or biological relevance.
  14. Grad-CAM sampling is representative rather than exhaustive. Each primary dataset/model set contains 25 deterministic cases.
  15. Grad-CAM maps are coarse and cross-model comparisons are not paired.
  16. Small error subgroups. Some outcome strata contain 1–6 examples; repeated-parent groups have only 2–3 errors.
  17. No stain/cell/padding segmentation in explainability. Spatial labels such as “background” are qualitative visual descriptions rather than segmented compartments.
  18. Historical package provenance is incomplete. Current ml_env and requirements-lock.txt are documented, but a full exact training-runtime package lock is not embedded in every fit.
  19. Pretrained checksum metadata is declared rather than runtime re-verified in this final audit. Timm identifiers and model parameter counts are enforced; the declared pretrained hashes should not be described as freshly verified cache hashes.

29. Exact claim boundaries¶

Scientifically supported claims¶

Supported wording Why it is justified
“ConvNeXtV2-Tiny had higher pooled OOF balanced accuracy and MCC than EfficientNet-B1 at every reported evaluation unit.” Directly supported by validated pooled OOF tables
“C-NMC used subject/group-disjoint development cross-validation.” Subject and final-group isolation verified across outer folds
“ALL-IDB1 used field-disjoint CV over 107 canonical fields.” Frozen field grouping and duplicate canonicalization
“ALL-IDB2 used parent-field-disjoint CV over crops mapped to canonical source fields.” Parent mapping and outer grouping verified
“Selected C-NMC ConvNeXt false negatives had higher peripheral/background CAM energy.” Outcome-stratified border diagnostic + contact-sheet review
“ALL-IDB1 attention frequently touched edges/padding or broad field areas.” Contact sheets and border diagnostics
“ALL-IDB2 EfficientNet selected errors had higher mean border fractions than selected TP cases.” Primary selected-set descriptive statistics
“Perfect ALL-IDB1 ConvNeXt performance occurred in a strongly acquisition-confounded dataset.” Perfect OOF metrics plus class-resolution association

Claims that are not scientifically justified¶

Do not claim Reason
“ALL-IDB1 is subject-disjoint.” Subject identity unavailable
“ALL-IDB2 is subject-disjoint.” Parent field is not a subject identifier
“ALL-IDB2 independently externally validates ALL-IDB1.” Shared source material/provenance
“ALL-IDB2 parent-field metrics are patient-level.” Parent is a source field, not a patient
“Perfect ALL-IDB1 performance proves morphology learning.” Severe acquisition/resolution confounding
“Grad-CAM proves which pixels caused the prediction.” Post-hoc gradient attribution is non-causal
“Grad-CAM identifies leukemia morphology.” No morphology annotation/segmentation or causal validation
“Fold SD is a confidence interval.” It is only sample SD of five fold metrics
“Fold SD measures seed uncertainty.” Only one seed was run
“ConvNeXt is better on every metric.” Counterexample: C-NMC cell NLL favors EfficientNet slightly
“Error CAMs target the true class.” They target the locked OOF predicted class
“Cross-model CAM differences are paired.” Selected cases mostly differ and geometries differ
“Current Grad-CAM source exactly regenerates all six primary trees.” ConvNeXt generated tolerance (0.001) differs from current hard-coded 0.05

30. Reproducibility guide¶

This is a record of how the completed experiment is defined; it is not an instruction to retrain during notebook review.

30.1 Reconstruct the scientific inputs¶

  1. Use the frozen C-NMC inventory/inspection/split artifacts under data/cnmc/.
  2. Use data/allidb1/allidb1_inventory.*, allidb1_eligibility_v1.json, and allidb1_splits_v1.json.
  3. Use data/allidb2/allidb2_inventory.*, allidb2_parent_map.csv, allidb2_eligibility_v1.json, and allidb2_splits_v1.json.
  4. Do not regenerate/freeze splits unless intentionally creating a new protocol version.

30.2 Reconstruct model/training semantics¶

Read the model YAMLs and factories, src/data/preprocessing.py, src/data/augmentation.py, src/training/trainer.py, src/training/artifacts.py, and src/training/protocol.py. Confirm seed 42, five folds, model identifiers, input sizes, phase LRs, weighted-CE formula, D4 training-only augmentation, AMP, patience, and checkpoint ranking.

30.3 Verify completed fits rather than rerun them¶

For each dataset/model/fold, validate fit_complete.json against its referenced checkpoint/history/metadata/OOF artifacts. The final repository contains 30 complete fit manifests. A representative manifest cryptographically binds the scientific checkpoint and OOF CSV by SHA-256.

30.4 Reconstruct reported performance¶

Use the existing outputs/predictions/**/oof_fold_*.csv together with the already-generated reports. The authoritative final comparison is md files/reports/final_model_comparison.md; complete per-fold metrics are in md files/reports/foldwise_metrics.md; curves are in reports/training_curves.csv; best epochs and overfitting assessments are in md files/reports/best_epoch_summary.md.

30.5 Reconstruct explainability interpretation¶

Use the generated outputs/gradcam/.../seed_42/ trees and md files/reports/gradcam_summary.md. Treat generated manifests/summaries as provenance authority for the completed CAM outputs, especially for ConvNeXt probability tolerance, because current run_gradcam_analysis.py differs from the ConvNeXt generation snapshot.

30.6 Environment¶

Do not silently replace the current environment with the separate requirements-lock.txt snapshot. If exact historical-runtime reproduction becomes a formal requirement, first establish a versioned environment manifest from archived training provenance rather than assuming equivalence.

Provenance anomalies intentionally retained¶

32. Final conclusions¶

  1. The project completed the intended experiment matrix: 30/30 seed-42 fits across three datasets, two architectures, and five outer folds, with OOF artifacts and completion metadata intact.
  2. Leakage control is a central scientific contribution of the workflow. C-NMC uses subject plus duplicate connectivity; ALL-IDB1 uses canonical field disjointness; ALL-IDB2 uses reconstructed parent-field disjointness. The split unit follows known relatedness rather than naïve image rows.
  3. ConvNeXtV2-Tiny is the preferred model inside this locked pipeline on pooled OOF balanced accuracy and MCC at every evaluation unit. This is not a universal superiority claim and does not identify the architectural reason.
  4. C-NMC shows strong but imperfect subject-aware generalization. ConvNeXt subject BA/MCC are 0.8547/0.7618 with very high ROC-AUC (0.9885), but specificity at threshold 0.5 is only 0.7308 and fold variability is meaningful. Both architectures show HIGH overfitting tendency.
  5. ALL-IDB1's perfect ConvNeXt result must be heavily qualified. The dataset contains strong resolution/acquisition confounding (33/33 eligible 1712×1368 fields are positive), so perfect OOF field classification does not prove morphology learning or transportability.
  6. ALL-IDB2 provides strong parent-aware internal evidence, not external validation. ConvNeXt crop BA/MCC are 0.9846/0.9691 and parent-field BA/MCC are 1.0/1.0, but ALL-IDB2 shares provenance with ALL-IDB1 and the parent field is not a patient.
  7. Grad-CAM supplies warning-oriented spatial diagnostics rather than causal explanations. Selected cases show background/edge/padding-associated patterns worth controlling in future experiments, but the maps do not establish disease-specific morphology learning.
  8. The next scientific step is not to overstate these results. Stronger claims require acquisition-balanced and genuinely independent external data, repeated seeds/repeated CV, and explainability analyses with explicit cell/stain/padding segmentation or controlled perturbation tests.

Bottom line: The evidence supports ConvNeXtV2-Tiny as the preferred architecture for this completed, leakage-aware, single-seed cross-validation study. The pipeline is technically auditable and internally well controlled for known duplicate/group leakage, while external validity, acquisition confounding, single-seed uncertainty, and non-causal explainability remain the key constraints on interpretation.

What my professor should remember¶

  • Training accuracy was calculated automatically at every epoch for all 30 completed fits. There was no missing training-accuracy calculation that required a separate script.
  • Inner-validation metrics selected the best checkpoint. They belong to model selection inside each outer-training partition and are not the final held-out result.
  • Outer-held-out OOF metrics are the primary generalization estimates. Each sample contributes one held-out prediction, and the five outer folds are concatenated for pooled OOF performance.
  • There is no separate fixed labeled external test cohort. C-NMC Final is unlabeled, C-NMC Preliminary was not used as a fresh final test set, and ALL-IDB1/2 were evaluated by leakage-aware cross-validation.
  • High training accuracy does not imply high generalization. C-NMC demonstrates the gap clearly and remains classified HIGH for overfitting tendency.
  • Evaluation units must remain dataset-specific. C-NMC supports subject-level aggregation, ALL-IDB1 is field-level, and ALL-IDB2 parent-field aggregation is not subject-level. ALL-IDB1 and ALL-IDB2 share source provenance and are not independent external validation cohorts.

Appendix C. Notebook execution safety¶

The code cells in this notebook are intentionally limited to read-only presentation operations: rendering schematics, plotting existing reports/training_curves.csv values, and displaying/downsampling existing Grad-CAM contact sheets. There is no call to a training script, trainer, optimizer, model factory, checkpoint loader, or model forward pass.

Protected scientific artifacts remain under data/, reports/, and outputs/. The notebook and its HTML export are the only final presentation artifacts created or modified by this synthesis step; protected scientific artifacts under data/, reports/, and outputs/ remain unchanged.
